zones.name: Public
zones.area: Ticket halls and the open concourse, before the fare gates.
zones.whoBelongs: Anyone off the street. Riders, buskers, pigeons, lost tourists.
zones.securityParallel: The public internet and the DMZ edge.
zones.description: Anyone can stand here, so trust nothing that happens here. The concourse is where trouble buys its ticket.

zones.name: Paid
zones.area: Platforms and trains, past the fare gates.
zones.whoBelongs: Riders who tapped a valid fare.
zones.securityParallel: The authenticated user network. You proved who you are, so now you may ride.
zones.description: One tap buys the platform. The turnstile is the only thing between order and a free-for-all.

zones.name: Staff
zones.area: Back rooms, mess rooms, and equipment closets inside a station.
zones.securityParallel: The internal corporate network behind the login.
zones.description: Staff only, in theory. In practice, a propped door and a confident nod get you a long way.

zones.name: Operational
zones.area: Depots, tunnels, signal cabins, and power rooms.
zones.whoBelongs: Operations and maintenance crews on shift.
zones.securityParallel: The restricted operational technology network that runs the machines.
zones.description: Where the heavy machinery lives. High voltage, moving trains, and safety rules written in blood.

zones.name: Control
zones.securityParallel: The management plane and the crown jewels.
zones.description: One room commands every train, signal, and gate. Guard it like the last slice of cake at a birthday party.

lines.name: Red Line
lines.description: The workhorse. Longest, busiest, and always a minute late. Runs coast to coast, Harbor to World's End.

lines.name: Blue Line
lines.description: The commuter's line. Reliable, tidy, and proud of it. Market to Bayside with no surprises and no fun.

lines.name: Green Line
lines.description: The scenic detour. Fewer stops, better views, and one permanently broken lift at Summit.

lines.name: Circle Line
lines.description: The loop that never ends. A gift to tourists, a curse to anyone trying to count laps.

stations.name: Harbor
stations.description: The end of the Red Line and the first coffee of the day. Salt air, loud gulls, and commuters who have not woken up yet.

stations.name: Market
stations.description: Where the Red and Blue lines shake hands. Two lines, one very confused tourist map, three buskers.

stations.name: Central
stations.description: The beating heart. Four lines cross here. If Central sneezes, the whole network catches a cold.

stations.name: Riverside
stations.description: Pretty views and damp platforms. The substation next door hums a note only dogs enjoy.

stations.name: World's End
stations.description: The last stop on the Red Line. Nobody means to come here. Everybody eventually does.

stations.name: Parkside
stations.description: Leafy, quiet, and faintly smug. The kind of station with strong opinions about litter.

stations.name: Bayside
stations.description: End of the Blue Line, start of the wind. Hold onto your hat and your fare card.

stations.name: Summit
stations.description: The high point of the Green Line, in altitude and in self-regard. The lift has been broken since spring.

stations.name: Junction
stations.description: Where Green meets the Circle. Trains loiter here and schedules come to die.

sites.name: Eastyard Depot
sites.description: Where trains sleep and mechanics swear. Badge in, or the guard dogs introduce themselves.

sites.name: Junction Signal Cabin
sites.description: A shed full of levers that decide who lives. Please do not touch the levers.

sites.name: Riverside Substation
sites.description: It hums, it sparks, it powers the line. It does not forgive a careless hand.

controlCenter.name: Operations Control Center
controlCenter.description: The brain of the network. One room runs every train, signal, and gate. If an attacker reaches this floor, the run is already lost.
